page.layout: One column of running text, with a short marginal note at the right beside the lines "Civitas in possessione" to "pariter in reb." Running head at top, page number top right, catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: ex hac provincia assessores sint if collegio« generalium ordinum, qui cum caeteris deliberandi & statuendi potestatem de rebus« foederis habeant, alter ex oppidanis, ex agrariis alter: unus item in ordinum senatu,« & unus in senatu rerum maritimarum, idq; alternatim, ita ut si iste ex urbe fuerit,« hic sit ex agro, & contra: Provincia pro« modo virium certam partem sustineat onerum, quae tuendo foederi sunt necessaria: in negotiis provincialibus aut communibus vno utatur sigillo ex urbano & agrario confecto. Civitas in consessibus & actionibus« nibus ac rebus omnibus priores partes« teneat, agrarij secundas: in suffragijs« tamen pares sint: quae si discrepent, delectis pari numero utraq; a parte permittatur res; qui & ipsi si nequeat consentire inter se, gubernator suffragio suo dissensione dirimat. Et hac ex partium consensu. De mercatus iure,& controversis rebus aliis sic, uti iudices, pronunciarunt.Sentia[?] Civitas in possessione« juris STAPVLÆ pariter in reb. in agro natis& peregrinis maneto: propolæ & propoliarundem III-viiorum, in agro non funto: de cerevisiæ usu res ma-« neto in eo statu, in quo solet ex foedere esse:« HOVEIMANNI[?] quoque ad iudicandas res« relinquuntur iidem, & eadem in potestate, qui & qua in potestate constituti sunt ab ordinum senatu statim in initio deditæ

page.notes: The page is a single column; the running head "IN FOED. BELG." and page number 141 are clear. Lines ending in « are printed as quotation marks at line ends. Marginal notes at right are small and partly illegible; the first is read as "Sentia[?]" and the second as "rundem III-viiorum," with doubt. "ifcollegio" (line 1) is uncertain and may be "in collegio" with a ligature. "HOVEIMANNI" is uncertain. Several words in the central lines are hard to read exactly (for example "funto:de" and "cerevisiae") and are transcribed as best read. The text is in a mixture of roman and small caps: "STAPVLÆ" is set in capitals. The catchword "Gro." sits at the bottom right.
